text:
# OF CHRIST, BOOK III.

<meta>continues from previous page: even now I do not cease to speak to all;</meta> but many are deaf to my voice and hard-hearted. More people listen to the world more willingly than to God; they follow the appetite of their flesh more easily than the good pleasure of God. The world promises temporal and small things, and it is served with great greed: I promise the highest and eternal things, and the hearts of mortals grow numb. Who serves and obeys me in all things with such care as the world and its masters are served? <margin>Isaiah 23</margin> Be ashamed, O Sidon <note>original: "Erubesce, Sidon"; a reference to the Phoenician city representing worldly pride and commerce</note>, says the sea. And if you ask the reason, hear why. For a meager stipend <note>original: "præbenda"</note>, a long journey is run; for eternal life, many hardly lift a foot once from the earth. A cheap price is sought; for a single coin <note>original: "numismate"</note>, people sometimes shamefully quarrel; for a vain thing and a small promise, they do not fear to grow weary day and night.

4. But, oh shame! for the unchangeable good, for the priceless reward, for the highest honor and unending glory, they are too lazy to be fatigued even a little. Blush then, lazy and complaining servant, that they are found readier for destruction than you are for life. They rejoice more in vanity than you do in truth. Indeed, they are sometimes frustrated in their hope; but my promise deceives no one, nor does it send away empty anyone who trusts in me. What I have promised, I will give; what I have said, I will fulfill; if only a person remains faithful in my love until the end. I am the rewarder of all good people, and the strong tester of all the devout.

5. Write my words in your heart and ponder them diligently; for they will be very necessary in the time of temptation. What you do not understand when you read, you will know in the day of visitation <note>original: "in die visitationis"; the moment of divine trial or the arrival of God's grace</note>. I am accustomed to visit my chosen ones in two ways: namely, by temptation and by consolation. And I read two lessons to them daily: one, by rebuking their vices; the other, by exhorting them to the increase of virtues. He who has my words and despises them has one who will judge him on the last day.

<note>Vocabulary: Sidon, world, eternal life, temptation, consolation, rewarder, the word of God.</note>

<summary>God rebukes those who exert more effort for worldly gain than for eternal life. He explains that he trains his chosen ones through a balance of discipline and comfort.</summary>
<keywords>devotion, worldly vanity, eternal life, divine trials, divine consolation, spiritual laziness, judgment</keywords>
